# ICharacterAttributes

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Fonts` · interface

```csharp
public interface ICharacterAttributes
```

Supplies the drawing attributes for each character of a string.

## Remarks

An implementation behaves like a cursor: [`MoveTo`](#moveto) positions it on a character of the original text, and the attribute members then describe that character. Positioning once and reading many attributes keeps the (potentially non-trivial) lookup out of each individual attribute.

The cursor is absolute (see [`CharacterCursor`](CharacterCursor.md)), so text that is drawn in several pieces shares one instance: no attribute splitting is required, characters that are never drawn simply are never visited, and a drawing pass can be repeated in any order. Implementations that cache their position must therefore tolerate a cursor that moves backwards.

Implementations are consumed through a generic constraint rather than as a boxed interface, so the per-character members are devirtualized and inlined. Additional attributes should be added as default interface implementations that describe the identity (no-op) value, which keeps existing implementations source compatible. NOTE: a `struct` implementation must implement every member explicitly, including the identity ones, because invoking a default interface implementation through a generic constraint boxes the value on every call.

## Properties

### Color

```csharp
Color? Color { get; }
```

Types: [`Color`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Color.md)

Gets the color that replaces the color passed to the draw method for the current character, or `null` to draw it in that color.

The color of the text belongs to the caller of the draw method, so an implementation that describes something other than color (a per-glyph translation, for example) leaves this alone and the text keeps the color it was drawn with.

### Rotation

```csharp
Angle Rotation { get; }
```

Types: [`Angle`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Angle.md)

Gets how far the current character is turned, about the middle of its advance on the baseline (see [`CharacterCursor.X`](CharacterCursor.md#x)). With [`Translation`](#translation) this is what sets text along a curve: each character moved onto the curve and turned to its slope.

### Translation

```csharp
Vector2 Translation { get; }
```

Gets how far the current character is moved from where the text puts it, in pixels of the font's native size, in the text's own space (before the text's scale and rotation).

Geometry, unlike color, applies to every layer: a character's shadow, glow, outline and face move as one. It takes no part in layout: text is measured and wrapped from the font's metrics alone, so a character moved far enough is outside the bounds measured for the text.

## Methods

### MoveTo

```csharp
void MoveTo(in CharacterCursor cursor)
```

Types: [`CharacterCursor`](CharacterCursor.md)

Positions the cursor on the specified character of the original text.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `cursor` | The position of the character within the original text. |

This is called once for each glyph that is drawn rather than once for each character of the text, so a character that draws nothing is skipped.
